phase_0.boundary_condition: electroweak symmetry breaking scale (246 GeV) — the Higgs vacuum expectation value that closes the weak interaction gauge structure and defines the neutrino mass scale

⊢.justification: the void state before any weak vertex exists; no lepton number, no flavor, no spacetime point assigned

⊣.justification: the closed boundary where SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y breaks to U(1)_EM; all weak processes terminate at this scale

≻.justification: forward morphism νₑ → e⁻ + W⁺ carrying weak isospin +1/2 → -1/2 transformation toward the electron final state

≺.justification: contravariant descent νₑ + Z⁰ → νₑ reversing momentum flow without flavor change; the antineutrino conjugate process

⋈.justification: composition of neutrino-W vertex followed by W-quark vertex in νₑ + n → p + e⁻; ordered chaining of two weak vertices

⊙.justification: the neutrino identifies itself via conserved U(1)_L charge; the stone that knows its own lepton number

∈.justification: one neutrino state opens into two arms: W-exchange (flavor-changing) and Z-exchange (flavor-conserving)

∋.justification: both current arms rejoin at the complete weak interaction vertex; conflicting flavor-change vs flavor-conserve fuse to B

⊤.justification: affirmative arm: charged current succeeds, electron produced, lepton number transferred visibly

⊥.justification: negative arm: only neutral current occurs, neutrino continues unchanged, no charged lepton appears

⊞.justification: paradice: flavor eigenstate (νₑ) and mass eigenstate (ν₁,ν₂,ν₃) held simultaneously; both true and false for definite flavor

⊡.justification: irreversible fixation: Cherenkov ring in water, scintillation pulse, or track in emulsion — permanent append-only measurement
